jobs.occupation: Research Scientist and Curator (m/f/d)  of the section Vertebrata (Tenure Track) (Biologe/Biologin)
jobs.description: Senckenberg Society for Nature Research (SGN), headquartered in Frankfurt am Main, is seeking to fill the following position at the Senckenberg Museum of Natural History in Görlitz, ideally as of April 1, 2027:Research Scientist and Curator (m/f/d) of the section Vertebrata (Tenure Track)(full time / part time options available)Location: GörlitzEmployment scope: full time / part time options are availableType of contract: initially limited to three years;the type of time limitation depends on individual profile and legal framework (maximum 3+3 years). A permanent employment is planned after a positive evaluationRemuneration: collective agreement of the German Länder, TV-L E13The Senckenberg Society for Nature Research is a member of the Leibniz Association and has been investigating the “Earth System” worldwide for more than 200 years, examining the past, analysing the present, and developing projections for the future. We conduct integrative geobiodiversity research with the aim of understanding nature in all its complexity and diversity in order to preserve it as the foundation of life for future generations and to ensure its sustainable use. Across eight institutes and five research stations throughout Germany, scientists from more than 40 countries conduct research at the highest international level.The renowned Senckenberg Museum of Natural History, located in the medieval town of Görlitz, combines research at an international level with extensive collections and an engaging museum programme. The surrounding Upper Lusatia region offers a large variety of opportunities for experiencing nature.Senckenberg is committed to study the causes and effects of biodiversity loss in the Anthropocene. As part of our strategic development, we launched an ambitious long-term research effort in “Anthropocene Biodiversity Loss” encompassing the modules “Collectomics”, “Biodiversity Genomics”, and “Solution Labs”. Objectives include the transformation of natural history collections into the digital era, studying biodiversity from the genome to the ecosystem levels and offering exploratory spaces for science and society to develop common solutions to Anthropocene challenges.For the Görlitz vertebrate collection, which comprises approximately 70,000 specimens (preserved using dry, cryogenic, and liquid preservation methods, with the focus on mammals; birds make up a smaller proportion, while other vertebrate groups represent only a small fraction), we are seeking an internationally recognized scientist with a solid track record in mammal research, possibly supplemented by work on another vertebrate groups.Potential research topics may include various aspects such as mammalian diversity, functional morphology, phylogeny, or biological interactions. Curation and collection-based research should play a significant role in the applicant’s research approach. The selected candidate should be open to research collaborations with SGN colleaguesYour tasks- Scientific curation and development of the vertebrate collection and the associated resources as an important international research infrastructure through international networking, growth, and improved accessibility.- Develop a visible portfolio of collection-based research with basic and applied aspects in the broad field of mammalogy and possibly other vertebrate groups by using a range of established and innovative methods and approaches.- Taking responsibility for the relocation of the collection items, including the infrastructure of the Mammalogy/Vertebrate Section, to the new campus at Bahnhofstraße 30 at Görlitz.- Secure external research funds.- Publish results of your research in international scientific outlets.- Establish collaborations with ongoing projects, regional and national (region (e.g., long-term projects on wolf, lynx) and international (e.g., Africa, Mongolia), including with other sections and departments in Görlitz and further Senckenberg institutes.- Communicate with external stakeholders such as scientific associations, conservation agencies, local and regional authorities, as well as citizen scientists.- Participate in teaching in the MSc level programmes of International Institute Zittau/ Dresden University of Technology.Your profile- Doctoral degree in biology/zoology or a related field- Expert knowledge of mammals, including native species (the biogeographic focus of the mammal collection is currently the Palearctic), additional expertise in other vertebrate groups- Proactive willingness to implement innovative research approaches, such as in the field of genomics, morphometrics, AI, imaging, 3D methods, pollutant analysis in a collection context- Ability to identify attractive research questions and make use of synergies through collaborations- Excellent academic track record adequate to your career stage- Experience in the acquisition of third-party funding and project management- Experience in supervising staff (doctoral candidates, BSc., MSc., students, technical staff), ability to work in a team- Very good command of German (B2)- Fluency in English, both spoken and written- Class B driving licence (international driving licence)- Willingness to travel on occasion to the extent possible considering your personal circumstancesDesirable skills- Knowledge in molecular, biochemical or biophysical techniques in taxonomy and ecology- Knowledge in research data management and databases- Experience in curation and management of zoological collections, and in museum workWe offer- Access to an international network of scientists, policymakers and research organizations- An attractive job within the inspiring and dynamic working environment of an internationally recognized research institution with excellent infrastructures and collaborations opportunities, e. g. in morphology, genomics, evolutionary biology, (paleo-)ecology- A working place in completely new building with dissection and other laboratories, collection rooms, in the historic town of Görlitz with rapidly developing local research community (DZA, CASUS, IHI/TUD, HiLusatia), yet situated very close to nature with high mammal diversity and opportunities for field work- Opportunities to participate in teaching and outreach activities, e.g., in our museum and with collaborating universities- Opportunities for establishing an independent academic working group and acquiring further academic qualifications- Flexible working hours – mobile working options – employee ID card with free admission to Senckenberg museums – annual special payment – collectively agreed vacation entitlement – company pension planSenckenberg is committed to diversity. We benefit from the different expertise, perspectives and personalities of our staff and welcome every application from qualified candidates, irrespective of age, gender, ethnic or cultural origin, religion and ideology, sexual orientation and identity or disability. Women are particularly encouraged to apply as they are underrepresented in the field of this position; in the case of equal qualifications and suitability, they will be given preference. Applicants with a severe disability will be given special consideration in case of equal suitability. Senckenberg actively supports the compatibility of work and family and places great emphasis on an equal and inclusive work culture.How to apply?Please upload your application (letter of motivation with a short description of your previous and current research foci, a CV, certificates of academic achievements, list of publications as well as letter(s) of recommendation, if available) as a single PDF file by November 10, 2026.https://www.senckenberg.de/de/stellenanzeigen/For data protection information on the processing of personal data as part of the application and selection process, please refer to the privacy policy on our homepage at https://www.senckenberg.de/en/imprint/For further information about the Senckenberg Gesellschaft für Naturforschung please visit www.senckenberg.deContactSenckenberg Gesellschaft für NaturforschungSenckenberganlage 2560325 Frankfurt a.M.For specific questions about this role please contact Prof. Dr. Hjalmar S. Kühl.E-Mail hjalmar.kuehl@senckenberg.de

GEOMAR Helmholtz Centre for Ocean Research Kiel is a foundation under public law jointly financed by the Federal Republic of Germany (90%) and the State of Schleswig-Holstein (10%). It is one of the internationally leading institutions in the field of marine research.Through our research and our commitment to the transfer of knowledge and technology, we contribute significantly to the preservation of the function and protection of the ocean for future generations.The research group Plankton Imaging Technology and Deep-Sea Zooplankton Ecology at GEOMAR (in cooperation with Kiel University’s Marine Data Science Group) is offering a position in the project “MegaRays - Deciphering Underwater Light Fields for 3D Plankton Characterization” starting at the earliest possible date.The position is offered for a duration of 3 years, with the possibility of extension. In the first year, the successful candidate will be employed by GEOMAR at 75%, supplemented by a 25% contract at Kiel University. Years two and three are fully funded at 100% (pay grade E13 according to the collective agreement for the public sector, TVöD, depending on experience).The position offers the opportunity to pursue a doctoral degree in natural or computer science as a member of the “Helmholtz School for Marine Data Science” (MarDATA). MarDATA’s interdisciplinary focus spans supercomputing, modeling, (bio)informatics, robotics, statistics, and big data methodologies. Doctoral researchers benefit from a structured training program that promotes cross-disciplinary collaboration and provides in-depth scientific insight as well as a systematic approach to marine data science. For more information, visit: https://www.mardata.de/. As part of the MarDATA doctoral network, the project “MegaRays - Deciphering Underwater Light Fields for 3D Plankton Characterization” aims at exploring the use of underwater light field cameras for observing and characterizing plankton organisms (zooplankton) in the ocean. Light field cameras deviate from off-the-shelf cameras in that all rays have to pass through an extra microlens array that changes their direction. Effectively, this means photographing the object from several slightly different perspectives, allowing focussing or 3D reasoning after image capture. The effects intertwine with refraction at the underwater housing and light-medium interaction in front of the camera.The successful applicant willcombine mathematical models for light field cameras and physical principles of refraction and underwater light propagation in order to simulate the image formation processemploy and extend methods of inverse rendering to visually reconstruct plankton from light field imagesdevelop workflows to extract ecological variables from light field imageryinvestigate, how automated classification can be improved by the extra 3D or raw information contained in light field imagesdevelop techniques for geometric co-calibration of light field images with a bioluminescence-sensitive camera in order to create 3D plankton models of bioluminescent deep-sea organismsIt is also expected that the successful applicant will create and contribute to creation and presentation of scientific publications, develop software for calibration, simulation and reconstruction, and is willing to perform and support data acquisition in the lab or at sea during scientific research cruises and collaborate with colleagues from other disciplines as well as the marine technology. Required:Master’s degree (or equivalent) in Computer Science or a related fielddocumented successful participation in classes in Computer VisionProfound knowledge in programmingAbility to use Computer Vision and Machine Learning libraries on HPC-machinesvery good English skills (written and spoken)If the university degree has not yet been completed at the time of application, credible evidence must be provided that the degree can be obtained by the start date spec...Homeoffice:Umfang: Nach Vereinbarung

conferences, write project reports.- Collaborate closely with researchers, data scientists, and industrial partners working on electrolyte synthesis, battery development, modelling, and scale-up.Your GEOMAR Helmholtz Centre for Ocean Research Kiel is a foundation under public law jointly financed by the Federal Republic of Germany (90%) and the State of Schleswig-Holstein (10%). It is one of the internationally leading institutions in the field of marine research.Through our research and our commitment to the transfer of knowledge and technology, we contribute significantly to the preservation of the function and protection of the ocean for future generations.The Research Unit Magmatic and Hydrothermal Systems (MuHS) of the research division 4 - Dynamics of the Ocean Floor is offering a position preferably starting as soon as possible. The position offers the possibility to attain a doctoral degree in natural sciences.The position is within the framework of the project “Understanding Core-Mantle Interaction Through Global Mapping of Ultra-Low Velocity Zones in Mantle Convection Models”, which is part of the German Science Foundation's Priority Programm SPP 2404 DeepDyn (https://www.geo.lmu.de/deepdyn/en/) about reconstructing the deep dynamics of planet Earth over geologic time.Ultra-Low Velocity Zones (ULVZs) are thin patches at the base of Earth’s mantle-only tens of kilometres high yet 100 to 1000 km wide-where seismic shear waves exhibit extreme reductions of 20-30%. They are archives of Earth’s thermochemical evolution, potentially reflecting its early differentiation or interactions with the core, but also more recent mantle flow patterns. Yet these interpretations depend critically on ULVZ composition, which remains poorly constrained.The doctoral researcher will numerically model ULVZ evolution and properties in plate-guided global mantle convection simulations. They will develop a framework that quantitatively evaluates these simulations by inferring ULVZ properties from mineral physics and comparing them to seismic constraints, including ULVZ geometry, geographic location and distribution. They will synthesize these results to deliver the first global ULVZ map based on dynamic simulations and to discriminate among proposed ULVZ compositions. Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz (JGU) is one of the largest universities in Germany. Thanks to its location in the Rhine-Main science region, the university can unfold to its full potential and showcase its innovative power and dynamism. Its status as a comprehensive university allows for multidisciplinary learning and teaching and has great potential for internationally renowned, interdisciplinary research. Almost all of its institutes are located on a single campus close to the Mainz city center - creating a lively academic culture for researchers, teaching staff, and students from every continent.Academic staff member (Postdoc): Plant RNA BiologyThe Wachter group investigates the molecular mechanisms and biological functions of alternative RNA splicing in plants (https://mps-imp.biologie.uni-mainz.de/). Our recent work has identified novel components of the plant splicing-regulatory code, including structured mRNA elements (e.g., https://doi.org/10.1111/tpj.71060 ) and position-dependent functions of pyrimidine motifs (https://doi.org/10.1111/tpj.16739). By combining these functional studies with global profiling approaches, we are building a framework to understand and engineer alternative splicing in the context of plant development and stress responses.As a member of our international research team, you will examine the regulation and functional impact of splicing decisions controlled by polypyrimidine tract-binding proteins (PTBs), a family of key splicing regulators in plants and animals. Your work will build on our previous findings on PTB functions in alternative splicing and on recent results from ongoing transcriptome-wide approaches, including splicing pattern profiling, iCLIP, and TRIBE. You will further develop these analysis pipelines and integrate the resulting datasets to define the role of this central component of splicing control in the model plant Arabidopsis thaliana. The new insights from these mechanistic studies will be linked to physiological PTB functions we previously observed, including ABA-dependent seed germination and drought tolerance. The overarching goal of this project is to establish the molecular connections between PTB functions and key traits of stress physiology, thereby laying the groundwork for novel strategies to enhance plant resilience. Who We Are 🌍Limatica measures what batteries whisper. We turn the tiny voltage noise of battery cells into a quality verdict, far faster than conventional tests, and help cell manufacturers cut scrap.We are a team of twelve in Chemnitz, spanning data, ML, HPC, hardware and industrialization. Early adopters across Europe and Asia already use our technology. In 2026 we move from pilots to production lines, and our data grows faster than our team.What You'll Do 🔧Our measurement stations produce several hundred GB of high-resolution voltage data per hour. You own the step from raw signal to reliable answer.- Work with novel cell noise data: Derive features from raw time series that make physical sense that hold up in production- Build for streaming: Design feature computations that work in streaming mode, at a throughput of up to 10,000 measurements per hour.- **Make throughput a design decision:**Build modular, parameterizable nodes for our distributed processing pipeline and help bring them into our Rust-based production environment.- **Ship modules, not scripts:**Automate evaluations end to end, from raw data to reports for our engineering team and our customers.- Own customer projects technically: Assess requirements, communicate interim results and findings, and turn feedback into improvements.What You Bring 🕵️- Measurement experience: A degree in electrical engineering (or comparable) and 3+ years with real-world measurement data. As we grow, this role can grow into technical lead.- Learn what few get to learn: Electrochemistry, Rust in production and data engineering at scale, with real cells and international manufacturers.- Share the upside: Salary package including virtual stock options.- Invest in yourself: Additional holiday for personal learning- Flexibility & wellbeing: Flexible hours, hybrid work, further benefits via Guud CardWhat it's like here: You get a lot of trust and a lot of room to shape things. We look for people who stay with a problem until it's solved and who enjoy the moments when a customer launch needs the whole team. Those are the moments where people here grow fastest. This role is intentionally a towards-senior position. You will take on increasing responsibility for pipeline modules and customer projects. jobs.occupation: Ph.D. student (m/f/x): Data analysis for exotic hadrons at hadronic thresholds (Physiker/in)
jobs.description: In order to fill a fixed-term position in part-time (26.2878 hours/week = 66%) at the earliest possible date, we are looking for 1Ph.D. student (m/f/x): Data analysis for exotic hadrons at hadronic thresholdsThe work of the chair of experimental physics 1 focuses on basic research: Oneof the most essential elements of todays education and research is to gain abetter understanding of the structure of matter and the fundamental principles ofnature. In this process the basic research of physics plays an important role as itprovides a base for technical innovations and development. Hadron Physicsdeals with strong interacting particles consisting of quarks and gluons. Amongthose hadrons also rank the building blocks of the atomic nucleus, the protonand the neutron. There are many other hadrons that can only be created viacollisions of high energetic particles in big particle accelerators. The created hadrons are detected by modern and complex detectors to examine their composition and interactions.The position is embedded in two research programs. DEMOS ("Democratizing Models") is an ErUM research initiative developing a federated, interoperable standard for describing, sharing and re-evaluating physics models across particle, hadron, nuclear, neutrino and astroparticle physics. Hadronic coupled-channel amplitudes are one of its flagship applications: they are analytically intricate and rarely reproducible from the publication alone, which makes them an ideal test case for the new standard. HADRON 2030 is an intercollaborative research network dedicated to studies of hadron physics. Within the ExHAT (Exploration of Heavy Hadrons at Thresholds) project, we will explore heavy hadrons at thresholds using spectroscopy methods with LHCb data and inclusive production studies with ALICE. The flagship case is the doubly charmed tetraquark Tcc(3875)+, which lies a fraction of an MeV below the D0D*+ threshold. Line shape, pole position, three-body DD-pi dynamics and isospin breaking have to be disentangled in a joint effort of theory and experiment.Scope: part-timeDuration: fixed-term, 3 yearsStart: at the earliest possible dateApply by:  2026-11-15Your tasks:- Application of advanced methods of data selection, efficiency and resolutionstudies within LHCb data analysis.- Construction, fitting and analytic continuation of coupled-channel scatteringamplitudes.- Decipherment and serialization of the complex amplitudes in the DEMOS / amplitude-serialization format.- Collaboration within the DEMOS / HADRON 2030 networks.- Exchange with the experimental collaborations [LHCb, BESIII, Belle II, GlueX, ...] and with EFT/lattice QCD groups.Your profile:- Master's degree (or equivalent) in physics, completed by the starting date.- Background in experimental particle physics or hadron physics, and familiarity with quantum field theory and scattering theory.- Good scientific programming skills (Julia, Python or C++) and experience with version control and reproducible workflows.- Very good command of written and spoken English.- Interest in working at the interface between theory and experiment and inopen, reusable research software.https://jobs.ruhr-uni-bochum.de/jobposting/cfcd29d29c6781afa43ea9ee698bf39148ca1c4f0?ref=AfA (https://jobs.ruhr-uni-bochum.de/jobposting/cfcd29d29c6781afa43ea9ee698bf39148ca1c4f0?ref=AfA)

internal and external stakeholders.- Experience in an administrative, executive support, banking, legal operations, paralegal, corporate services or similar coordination role.- Strong organisation and follow-through, with the confidence to chase people, manage deadlines and keep multiple workstreams moving.- Experience handling confidential information and formal documentation with accuracy and discretion.- Comfort working with banks, lawyers, advisers, notaries, corporate service providers or other external stakeholders.- Ability to work independently, prioritise changing requests and administration.Nice to have- Professional proficiency in French.- Experience supporting a CFO, finance leader, executive team or European corporate function.- Experience in a bank, financial CASA aims to strengthen the resilience of our digital society. The emergence of disruptive technologies in recent years, especially artificial intelligence and quantum computers, has caused substantial new challenges for cybersecurity research. In the second funding phase, CASA will specifically address these challenges. Thematic priorities include the security of quantum technologies, protection against Al-based disinformation and societal polarization, and new approaches to defending against ransomware. In addition to technical questions, it also investigates the interaction of human behavior and cybersecurity. Research at CASA, which is based at the Horst Görtz Institute for IT Security, follows a strongly interdisciplinary approach. Researchers from the fields of computerscience, cryptography, electrical engineering, mathematics, and psychology work together in an unique constellation in Europe. This holistic approach is unparalleled and holds the potential for scientific breakthroughs. Ruhr-University Bochum (RUB) and its Faculty of Computer Science offer an excellent environment for aspiring young researchers. 20 years ago, the Horst Görtz Institute for IT Security (HGI) was founded here. lt is now one of Europe's most prestigious institutions for basic computer security research. The HGI maintains extensive networks with leading research institutions worldwide and with media and industry. Moreover, it has produced numerous successful security startups. Governance & Risk Management* Maintain and continuously improve insurance tax governance and compliance frameworks.* Design and oversee internal control systems for insurance premium tax processes.* Contribute to the enhancement of DHL Group's Tax Compliance Management System.* Conduct risk assessments and compliance reviews related to insurance distribution and taxation.* Promote transparency, documentation standards, and audit readiness across the organization.  Regulatory & Audit Management* Manage insurance premium tax audits and regulatory reviews independently.* Act as the primary contact for tax authorities, auditors, legal advisors, insurers, and brokers.* Develop strategies to address audit findings and mitigate regulatory risks.* Monitor developments in German and international insurance tax legislation and relevant court decisions.* Ensure regulatory awareness and compliance regarding insurance distribution activities in Germany. Cross-Functional Collaboration* Work closely with colleagues from Tax, Legal, Treasury, Procurement, Risk Management, and other business functions.* Support DHL business units in understanding and meeting insurance compliance requirements.* Coordinate with external advisors, brokers, insurers, and regulatory stakeholders across multiple jurisdictions. What You Bring* University degree in Law, Tax, Business Administration, Finance, Insurance, Risk Management, or a related field.* Several years of professional experience in insurance taxation, insurance regulation, compliance, risk management, legal, or related disciplines.* Proven expertise in German Insurance Premium Tax (IPT) regulations and insurance compliance requirements.* Experience managing regulatory inquiries, audits, disputes, and complex multinational insurance programs.* Strong understanding of commercial insurance products, including Property, Liability, Marine, Cargo, Cyber, D&O, Financial Lines, and Employee Benefits.* Experience developing governance, control, and compliance frameworks in international organizations.* Excellent English language skills and good German language proficiency. You thrive in international settings, communicate effectively, and maintain the highest standards of integrity and quality. What We Offer* A highly visible role with global impact across one of the world's leading logistics companies.* Exposure to complex international insurance, tax, and compliance topics.* Opportunities to collaborate with senior stakeholders across multiple functions and regions.* A diverse, inclusive, and collaborative working environment.* Continuous professional development and career growth opportunities within DHL Group.(Employer value proposition formulated based on the role's global scope and responsibilities.) We value diverse perspectives and believe that our people are the key to our success. Employment decisions are based on qualifications, skills, experience, and performance. Your benefits * Well-Being: Fun, team spirit, and health are crucial factors. jobs.occupation: IMPACT PORTFOLIO MANAGER (Fairer Futures Programmes) (Projektleiter/in / Projektmanager/in)
jobs.description: Overview:Fairtrade is the most recognized and trusted sustainability label, working to make trade fairer for people and planet.For more than three decades, Fairtrade has been making an impact on the way trade works. We believe that every farmer and worker should have access to a better way of doing business, and a better way of living. Fairtrade International is an independent non-profit organisation representing more than two million small-scale farmers and workers worldwide. It owns the FAIRTRADE Mark, a registered trademark that appears on more than 37,000 products. Beyond certification, Fairtrade International and its member organisations (three producer networks and 19 national Fairtrade organisations) partner with producers and businesses, engage consumers, and advocate for a fair and sustainable future.Unit’s description and purpose: The Global Impact unit strengthens the Fairtrade system by driving institutional learning and effectiveness through robust monitoring and evaluation systems. We are the hub for the analysis and communication of high-quality data and information about Fairtrade and its impact, as well as supporting strategy delivery. The unit includes the Monitoring, Evaluation, and Learning (MEL) team, which is the Fairtrade system’s hub for MEL which directly connects evidence to strategic decision for the Global Strategy, individual Fairtrade projects and global programmes, Standards, producer support, and more.PRINCIPAL ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:Role purpose: The Impact Portfolio Manager (Fairer Futures Programmes) is responsible for stewarding the MEL frameworks for several of Fairtrade’s global product programmes, the flagship programmatic vehicles through which Fairtrade delivers measurable impact for farmers and workers under its 2026–2028 Global Strategy. The manager will share responsibilities for a total of three programmes (cocoa, banana, coffee) with another manager, with product- and thematic-specific focus to be determined upon hire.Working in close collaboration with Fairtrade Producer Networks, Global Product Teams, and the Digital Service Unit, the role ensures that both programmes are underpinned by robust, coherent, and actionable MEL, from framework design through data collection, reporting, evaluation, and learning. The position serves as one of Fairtrade International's primary MEL contact across programme discussions, representing the Global Impact unit in a system that spans FI, National Fairtrade Organizations, and Producer Networks. This role also contributes to the Global Impact unit's impact services offer, drawing on programme MEL expertise to identify and develop customized services for the Fairtrade system and external partners.Main Responsibilities:            - MEL Framework, Indicators, and Data Management. Steward and drive the development, maintenance, and continuous improvement of the Theory of Change and MEL framework for several of the Fairer Futures Programmes, working in close collaboration with Producer Networks and Global Product Teams. Steward the KPI and activity/output indicator set for both programmes, including maintaining metadata and monitoring data quality. OVERVIEW:Fairtrade is the most recognized and trusted sustainability label, working to make trade fairer for people and planet.For more than three decades, Fairtrade has been making an impact on the way trade works. We believe that every farmer and worker should have access to a better way of doing business, and a better way of living. Fairtrade International is an independent non-profit organisation representing more than two million small-scale farmers and workers worldwide. It owns the FAIRTRADE Mark, a registered trademark that appears on more than 37,000 products. Beyond certification, Fairtrade International and its member organisations (three producer networks and 19 national Fairtrade organisations) partner with producers and businesses, engage consumers, and advocate for a fair and sustainable future. Unit’s description and purpose: Global Products, Programs and Policy (GPPP) provides leadership to the Fairtrade system with selected product, program and policy intelligence. To this end GPPP provides information, tools and strategic direction as the main outputs. GPPP facilitates and contributes to coherent implementation of strategic plans within the Fairtrade system. GPPP develops new ways of delivering Fairtrade’s intended impact in a changing business environment and risk context.PRINCIPAL ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:Role purpose: The Cocoa Manager is responsible for implementation of GPPP cocoa works based on work schedule agreed with the Senior Advisor Cocoa. The work will deliver measurable impact for farmers and workers under its 2026–2028 Global Strategy. The Cocoa Manager joins a team that works fluidly, sharing responsibilities across multiple workstreams supporting each other where the need is the greatest to achieve their objectives. The environment is dynamic and priorities can shift with external events impacting workplans.  In addition to other duties the Cocoa Manager, working within GPPP cocoa, will  work in close collaboration with Producer Networks, National Fairtrade Organisations and the Fairtrade International Global Impact team responsible for Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning, to ensure the Fairer Futures Programme – West Africa Cocoa is implemented professionally and on time. The programme is primarily focused on increasing the household income of farmers who are members of Small Producer Organisaitons in the programme. The programme leads to farm level interventions through Small Producer Organisaitons including pruning, cocoa tree planting and shade tree planting among others. The programme includes further interventions on income such as Village Savings and Loans Association, and interventions on social compliance including increasing the effectiveness of child labour monitoring, reporting and remediation. Future working responsibilities may extend to other geographies and other commodities.Main Responsibilities:            - Supporting National Fairtrade Organisations, in their responsibilities to maintain and grow the market for Fairtrade cocoa.- Supporting Producer Networks, in their work with Small Producer Organisations, and maintaining and growing the market for Fairtrade cocoa.- Programme design. Work with stakeholders, and mostly importantly the Producer Network, to ensure programme design is based on evidence with robust monitoring, evaluation and learning contributing to the evolution of the programme.- Programme implementation. Co-management with the Producer Network based on agreed reporting structures and formats providing oversight and reporting to stakeholders in a timely manner. This will include the running of, and reporting to, a working committee.- Financial reporting.  Responsible for ensuring timely quarterly financial reporting including an understanding of any variance from plan and agreed actions to remediate that situation.- Programme monitoring, evaluation and learning. Working with Fairtrade International monitoring, evaluation and learning experts and the Producer Network to ensure implementation and prioritisation of effective monitoring, evaluation and learning in a timely manner.- External programme reporting. Working with Fairtrade International monitoring, evaluation and learning experts, Producer Network and National Fairtrade Organisations ensuring agreed reporting deadlines are met with quality reporting to be used with commercial stakeholders, government and other interested stakeholders.- External stakeholder engagement, traders. Working closely with the Producer Network manage relationships with exporter, importer and processers of cocoa who purchase Fairtrade cocoa from Small Producer Organisaitons. Traders are a critical part of the supply chain and their incorporation into the programme is desired and necessary.- External stakeholder engagement, events. Working with National Fairtrade Organisations you will be speaking at public and trade events on the strategic objectives of our work, the progress and impact with the aim of influencing the sector.- External stakeholder engagement, media. Where required you will interact with media.- Fairtrade Standards and Pricing. Liaising with the lead department in Fairtrade on standards and pricing, Fairtrade’s Standards Unit and Pricing Unit, you will be working on standards and pricing matters relating to Fairtrade’s cocoa work and the programme. This will include and not limited to consultations, queries and evolution of standards and pricing. You’ll be part of self-organizing, multicultural teams that collaborate in an agile setup.- People development: when you grow so do we!We want you to become the best version of yourself with individual and company-wide programs and trainings for people development. Focused among other on development, leadership, appreciation ... it´s time to upskill your career.- Support with individual solutions: we are people-caring!We offer support whenever you need it - at every stage of your professional journey.Want to know more about all our benefits? Discover more here (https://metro.digital/about/life-at-metro) .Let´s connect soon. Apply for the role now!Position grade within our career framework: Technical Architect Grade 1 (Md8).

The Leibniz-Institut für Analytische Wissenschaften - ISAS - e. V. develops efficient analytical methods for health research. Thus, it contributes to the improvement of the prevention, early diagnosis, and therapy of diseases like cardiovascular diseases or cancer. Overall, the institute strives to advance precision medicine by combining knowledge from different fields such as biology, chemistry, computer science, medicine, pharmacology, and physics. ISAS is a member of the Leibniz Association and is publicly funded by the Federal Republic of Germany and its federal states.We invite applications for the Research Group Biofluorescence: PhD candidate (f/m/d)This project, funded by the DFG as part of CRC 1752, "DYNAMO: Immediate Tumor Dynamics in Melanoma Therapy“ (https://www.uni-due.de/crc1752/) seeks to combine high-resolution multi-omics profiling, advanced computational modeling, and clinically aligned biomarker stratification, in order to generate actionable, patient-specific predictions and resistance-targeting interventions in melanoma therapy. You will be responsible for finding out the role of neutrophils for the early development of therapy resistance in human melanoma. The project is being carried out in collaboration with University Hospital Essen and the University of Duisburg-Essen.You will be responsible for- Experimental setup and execution of neutrophil functional profiling in the context of melanoma immune regulation and immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) response- Functional assays of neutrophils including migration, phagocytosis, and ROS production- Optimization and standardization of neutrophil functional assays for primary human samples- Few-cell proteomics for deep molecular characterization of neutrophil subsets- Multicolor flow cytometry of PBMCs and immune cell populations- Live-cell imaging and advanced microscopy for dynamic immune cell behavior analysis- Planning and execution of stimulation and inhibition experiments to dissect signaling pathways regulating neutrophil function in the melanoma context- Data processing, analysis, interpretation, and visualization of experimental results in collaboration with computational partnersYour profile- Completed diploma or master’s degree in molecular biology, cancer biology, immunology, cell biology, bioinformatics, translational medicine or related disciplines- Experience in molecular and cellular biology techniques, ideally with hands-on experience with functional immune cell assays (preferably with neutrophils or myeloid cells) is an advantage- Strong interest in melanoma biology, tumor immunology, immune checkpoint therapy, translational cancer research, and tumor–immune interactions- Experience with cell culture, flow cytometry, microscopy, proteomics workflows or high-dimensional immune profiling approaches is desirable- Experience with bioinformatics or biostatistics is beneficial but not required- Ability to work independently and in interdisciplinary teams, with strong organizational skills and analytical thinking- High level of self-motivation, scientific curiosity, reliability, creativity, and team-oriented personality with enthusiasm to work in a collaborative research environment- Fluent in spoken and written EnglishWe offer- A clear research topic as well as multifold training and support for PhD students in framework of ISAS and the Leibniz association- Opportunities for scientific training and development in an international environment and an excellent working atmosphere in a very dynamic and professional team- Access to state-of-the-art technologies including few-cell proteomics, high-dimensional flow cytometry, and advanced microscopy platforms- Integration into an interdisciplinary, internationally visible, translation-oriented cancer immunology research network- The opportunity to present your data on international conferences and participate in workshops- A wide range of opportunities for further training and qualifications- Flexible working times, mobile working and attractive social benefits- Family-friendly infrastructure and support from a family serviceNon-residents who apply for this job will receive help from the institute to find accommodation and to handle authorities. Applications from disabled applicants are welcome. ISAS supports the principle of equal opportunity for all employees and therefore particularly encourages women to apply.The part-time position (65%) starts on October 1, 2026, and is offered until June 30, 2030. The salary will be according to the German TV-L and falls within the pay group 13. The time limitation of the contract is based on the Wissenschaftszeitvertragsgesetz (WissZeitVG).ISAS collects and processes the personal data of its applicants in accordance with European and German legal regulations. Further information on data protection and the processing of personal data can be found at: https://www.isas.de/en/datenschutz.The closing date for applications is** August 14, 2026**. Please apply via our applicant portal (https://bewerbermanagement.net/en/jobposting/4e342c0b4ebdda805ec07aefc033c1e6bce0d9010/apply?ref=Agentur+f%C3%BCr+Arbeit+Dortmund) . If you have any questions (reference number 411_2026), feel free to contact the Human Resources team (bewerbungen@isas.de). Further information about the institute can be found at: https://www.isas.de/en.

As Platform Lead PTP/Banking in the SHAPE+ team, you will play a pivotal role in shaping and driving our global SAP S/4HANA Finance platform for Procure-to-Pay (PTP) and Banking processes. University Degree in Business Informatics (or similar), superior English skills (German a plus) and relocating to the Bonn/Cologne area, if necessary.  Who suits us? candidates already based in Germany (or nearby EU countries) are strongly preferred.Contact:Yannick Bartschhr@interzero.deErgänzende Informationen:Anforderungen an den Bewerber: Grundkenntnisse: Softwarearchitektur, Software testenErweiterte Kenntnisse: Datenbankadministration, -management, -organisation, REST (Representational State Transfer), Java Persistence API (JPA), Backend-Entwicklung, Programmiersprache Java

Applicants are invited for a double degree PhD fellowship/scholarship at Graduate School of Technical Sciences, Aarhus University, Denmark, within the Biological and Chemical Engineering programme. The position is available from 01 January 2027 or later. You can submit your application via the link under 'how to apply'.

The position is part of the MSCA project TagTIC - Target mining for the development of therapeutics against pathogen-induced cancers, ID: 101311627, Call: HORIZON-MSCA-2025-DN-01-01. Project website: tagtic.eu

Note that this is a double degree PhD project within an MSCA Joint Doctorate. Under the currently planned arrangement, the candidate will work for approximately three years at TissueGnostics GmbH in Vienna, Austria, and one year at Aarhus University, Denmark.

Research area and project description:

Microbial infections are increasingly recognized as important contributors to cancer, but identifying the spatial tissue features and molecular signatures associated with infection-driven disease remains challenging. Integrating tissue imaging with spatial transcriptomics and microbiome information offers opportunities to characterize disease-associated patterns and improve biomarker discovery.

Consortium: This PhD postion is part of the interdisciplinary TagTIC consortium, which brings together expertise in microbiology, virology, oncology, immunology, medicinal chemistry, imaging, AI, and bioinformatics, with support from associated partners in biotech, diagnostics, and science communication. Its collaborative structure allows doctoral candidates to work within a network where discovery science, technology development, training, and societal impact are closely connected.

Project DC11: This PhD is part of the TagTIC consortium. It combines machine learning with image analysis to support precision oncology. The aim is to develop AI algorithms that integrate tissue imaging, spatial transcriptomics and microbiome data (multiomics) to identify biomarkers and predict disease progression.

Project description: For technical reasons, you must upload a project description. Please simply copy the project description above and upload it as a PDF in the application.

Applicants to the PhD position must have a relevant master's degree in biology, biotechnology, molecular medicine, biomedicine, microbiology, cancer biology, bioengineering, bioinformatics or a closely related field.

At Genmab, we are dedicated to building extra[not]ordinary® futures, together, by developing antibody products and groundbreaking, knock-your-socks-off KYSO antibody medicines® that change lives and the future of cancer treatment and serious diseases. We strive to create, champion and maintain a global workplace where individuals’ unique contributions are valued and drive innovative solutions to meet the needs of our patients, care partners, families and employees.

Our people are compassionate, candid, and purposeful, and our business is innovative and rooted in science. We believe that being proudly authentic and determined to be our best is essential to fulfilling our purpose. Yes, our work is incredibly serious and impactful, but we have big ambitions, bring a ton of care to pursuing them, and have a lot of fun while doing so.

Does this inspire you and feel like a fit? Then we would love to have you join us!

**About The Role

**Genmab is seeking a Project Manager CMC Product Lifecycle Management to

• join the CMC Life Cycle Management (LCM) Team and support our growing portfolio of commercial products globally.

The LCM team is responsible for managing the CMC lifecycle activities of Genmab’s commercial products and manufacturing oversight, ensuring supply continuity, regulatory compliance, and successful execution of post-approval activities throughout the product lifecycle. In this role, you’ll work closely with LCM Product Lead and colleagues across Commercial Supply Chain, MSAT, Regulatory CMC, Commercial QA and External Manufacturing to ensure seamless execution of lifecycle management activities.

The CMC Life Cycle Management Team is part of CMC Project & Portfolio Management (PPM) which also includes the Early-Stage Development, Late-stage Development and External Manufacturing teams. CMC Project & Portfolio Management resides within CMC Development and Manufacturing, based in Denmark.

This role offers a unique opportunity to contribute to the continued growth of Genmab's commercial portfolio while working in a highly collaborative and cross-functional environment at the interface of development, manufacturing, supply, and regulatory affairs.

**Responsibilities

**

• Work alongside the LCM Lead to provide manufacturing oversight and execute lifecycle activities for an assigned manufacturing track (DS, BI, CI or DP) after commercial launch, supporting batch release and reliable supply. The LCM Lead retains overall product accountability.

• Lead operational governance with internal functions and partners/CMOs, aligning priorities, preparing decisions, tracking progress and actions, and providing input on CMO performance.

• Collaborate with internal and external stakeholders on daily operations to ensure manufacturing oversight (ie. Deviation management, change control, complaint handling, etc) , support batch release and supply, issues resolution/escalation and quality/regulatory compliance.

• Coordinate technical issue resolution and manage track risks with relevant experts, ensuring required assessments, documentation and mitigation actions, and escalating issues with proposed next steps.

• Drive manufacturing changes, projects and improvements within agreed scope, timelines and budgets.

• Support implementation of CMC commitments and Post-approval change management related to assigned product manufacturing track (i.e DS, BI, CI, DP) and support coordination of submission documentation preparation across stakeholders and CMOs/Partners.

• Support initiatives to optimize yield, reduce cost of goods, and enhance robustness of manufacturing and testing processes

• Help establish and improve LCM processes, governance, tools and ways of working, incorporating lessons learned.

**Requirements

**

• Master's degree in science or related technical discipline (e.g. engineering, biotech, pharmaceutical, biochemistry, biology) or equivalent experience;

• 4+ years of experience in biopharmaceutical industry, preferably within manufacturing operations, lifecycle, product management for commercial products.

• Experience in building relations and influencing multi-functional teams within multicultural organizations.

• Proven track record in CMC project management, manufacturing operations management or product management across development and commercialization activities.

• Experience managing and defining project coordination activities and tasks in a structured, regulated environment.

• Prior experience with commercial product lifecycle management and oversight of Contract Manufacturing Organizations (CMOs) is considered an advantage.

• Broad understanding of global cGMP requirements and regulatory expectations across major markets

• Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills, with fluency in English

• Demonstrated ability to work effectively in cross-functional and multicultural environments

• Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities, balance competing demands, and deliver against project timelines

• Team player with the ability to collaborate with diverse stakeholders.

• Result- and goal-oriented, committed to contributing to Genmab’s success

The proposed gross annual/hourly base salary range for this position, in the primary location, based on a full time schedule is:

DKK597.312,00---895.968,00

The final salary offer will depend on several factors, including your skills, qualifications, and experience.

In addition to base salary, this position is eligible for additional forms of compensation, such as discretionary bonuses and long-term incentives.

**Benefits

**When you join Genmab, you become a part of a culture that supports your physical, financial, social, and emotional well-being. Our benefits include, but are not limited to:

• Pension

• Health insurance and wellness benefits

• Paid time off

• Employee support programs

Further details on eligibility for compensation and benefits based on the role will be provided during the recruitment process.

**About Genmab

**Genmab is an international biotechnology company with a core purpose to improve the lives of patients through innovative and differentiated antibody therapeutics. For 25 years, its hard-working, innovative and collaborative team has invented next-generation antibody technology platforms and harnessed translational, quantitative and data sciences, resulting in a proprietary pipeline including bispecific T-cell engagers, antibody-drug conjugates, next-generation immune checkpoint modulators and effector function-enhanced antibodies. By 2030, Genmab’s vision is to transform the lives of people with cancer and other serious diseases with Knock-Your-Socks-Off (KYSO®) antibody medicines.

Established in 1999, Genmab is headquartered in Copenhagen, Denmark with international presence across North America, Europe and Asia Pacific. For more information, please visit Genmab.com and follow us on LinkedIn and X.

Genmab is committed to protecting your personal data and privacy. Please see our privacy policy for handling your data in connection with your application on our website Job Applicant Privacy Notice (genmab.com).

Senior D365 F&O Business/Functional Consultant

• Permanent contract

• Full-time

• At least 5 years of experience (Senior level)

• Bachelor degree

• IT

Mission

**Do you want to help shape the future of supply chain operations at the world’s leading maritime supplier of provisions and stores?**Do you have extensive knowledge of Microsoft Dynamics 365 Finance & Operations and a deep understanding of end-to-end supply chain processes, from Sales and Procurement to Warehouse and Logistics? Are you ready to take the lead in shaping and optimizing our global supply chain processes, turning business requirements into effective D365 F&O solutions?

If you are a business-oriented D365 F&O specialist who enjoys engaging with stakeholders, asking the right questions and constructively challenging existing ways of working, this could be the opportunity for you.

Become part of our ERP team in Nørresundby, DenmarkWith reference to our Team Lead, Kim Faarbæk, you will become part of our ERP team, working closely with business stakeholders and IT colleagues across our international organization.

As a Senior D365 F&O Business/Functional Consultant, your primary focus will be the full Supply Chain area in Microsoft Dynamics 365 Finance & Operations, covering order-to-cash, procure-to-pay, warehousing, inventory and logistics. You will be involved throughout the entire project lifecycle, from requirements gathering and solution design to testing, training, go-live and post-production support.

Senior D365 F&O Business/Functional Consultant with a focus on Supply Chain ManagementYou will play a key role in shaping and implementing our global D365 F&O solution. Working closely with business stakeholders, developers and ERP specialists, you will translate business requirements into functional designs and sustainable system solutions, while sharing best practices and driving process improvements.

You will also be involved in our transition from Microsoft Dynamics AX 2012 to D365 F&O, giving you the opportunity to influence solution design and shape future global processes across Sales, Procurement, Warehouse and Logistics. Through workshops and stakeholder collaboration, you will help deliver harmonized solutions that support our future growth and operational efficiency.

**

More specifically, your key responsibilities will be to:**

• Lead the configuration and implementation of core D365 F&O Supply Chain modules, including Sales, Procurement, Inventory, Warehouse and Transportation Management.

• Configure and optimize end-to-end supply chain processes across order-to-cash, procure-to-pay, warehousing, inventory and logistics.

• Advise on supply chain process improvements, with a focus on standard D365 functionality, inventory optimization and process harmonization.

• Gather, analyse and document business requirements, translating them into functional designs, user stories, acceptance criteria and system configurations.

• Develop functional design documentation for customizations, integrations, reports and system enhancements.

• Plan and execute testing activities, including system integration testing (SIT), user acceptance testing (UAT) and data validation.

• Collaborate with developers, architects and ERP specialists on integrations, customizations, data migration from AX 2012 and issue resolution.

• Lead workshops and training sessions, support implementation and user adoption, and share D365 F&O best practices to drive continuous improvement across the organization.

Profile

**Qualifications & requirements

**You bring extensive knowledge of Microsoft Dynamics 365 Finance & Operations, supported by several years of hands-on implementation experience. You have a strong understanding of end-to-end supply chain processes across Sales, Procurement, Inventory, Warehouse and Logistics. You are comfortable engaging with stakeholders at all levels, constructively challenging requirements and translating business needs into clear, functional solutions.

Furthermore, we expect that you have:

• 3+ years of experience as a functional consultant implementing Microsoft Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management (D365 F&O).

• Extensive functional knowledge of core D365 F&O modules, including Sales, Procurement, Inventory, Warehouse and Transportation Management.

• Proven experience with end-to-end order-to-cash and procure-to-pay processes, as well as inbound, outbound, warehousing and inventory processes.

• Experience with advanced Supply Chain modules such as Master Planning, Production Control, or Quality Management.

• Experience with requirements gathering, process mapping, functional design, configuration, testing and implementation.

• Experience with customizations, integrations, data entities, workflows, security roles and data migration.

• Strong stakeholder management and communication skills in English, with experience leading workshops and collaborating across functions and cultures.

• A structured and delivery-focused approach, with attention to quality, documentation and agreed deadlines.

**

It is an advantage if you have:**

• Experience in distribution, logistics, manufacturing or other asset-driven industries.

• Microsoft Certified: Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management Functional Consultant Associate certification.

• Experience with the Power Platform, including Power BI, Power Automate and Power Apps.

• Experience with EDI, system integrations or warehouse automation solutions.

• A relevant bachelor's degree, e.g. in Supply Chain Management, Business or IT.

**

Personality matters

**You are curious, analytical and collaborative, with a natural ability to engage with people and build strong relationships across the business and IT. You enjoy asking the right questions, challenging existing processes and finding practical solutions to complex business needs. You communicate clearly, take ownership and thrive in an international environment where knowledge-sharing, teamwork and continuous improvement are key.

**

We offer more than just a job

**We wish to be the best at what we do, and everything we do is based on our values of “Winning Attitude, Customer Orientation, and Getting it Done”. We offer flexible working hours and numerous employee benefits, counting a healthy canteen, take-away, free fruit, and fitness facilities. Wrist supports local elite sports, offering tickets to home games. You can expect free parking and access to Clever EV charging stations. Moreover, we have an active employee association that invites us all to play paddle, badminton, board games etc. and to join the yearly DHL relay race.

**

Ready to apply?

**Please send us your application and CV via the “Apply” button no later than 16. November 2026. We want to fill the position as soon as possible and will continuously invite candidates for interviews, so do not hesitate to submit your application and CV.

If you have questions or want to know more about the team, please reach out to Team Lead, Kim Faarbæk, at kifa@wrist.com or by phone on +45 2097 3050

**

At Wrist, we are committed to cultivating a culture of belonging where every individual feels seen, valued, and respected

**As a global company, we aim to reflect the communities we are part of, believing that our strength comes from diverse perspectives, experiences, and the unique contributions each person offers. We welcome applications from all qualified candidates, and we are dedicated to maintaining a recruitment process that is inclusive, fair, and respectful. By fostering a supportive workplace culture rooted in belonging, we lay the foundation for meaningful collaboration and shared success.

**

About Wrist

**Wrist is the world’s leading ship and offshore supplier of marine provisions and stores with a market share of approximately 12%. We are the only provisions and stores marine supplier with a global network of supply operations. We also offer services within owners’ goods and spare parts logistics, combining provisions and stores deliveries directly to the vessels. With the launch of the digital marketplace, Source2Sea, Wrist is leading the digital transformation of the marine supply industry. All year round, we offer 24/7 global online sourcing and logistics, providing data transparency, automation, and convenience to our customers. We continuously work on reducing our climate impact while at the same time proactively addressing our customers’ growing demand and need for responsible solutions and services. From more than 30 locations worldwide, in all major shipping locations, 1,800 Wrist employees take pride in making it easy for our customers to order and receive marine supplies and services.

About Spirii

Spirii is a full-service e-Mobility provider, offering hardware and software charging solutions to companies in the private and public sector. Spirii recently celebrated its seven-year anniversary as a founded company — though the people at Spirii bring far more extensive experience working with electric cars and charging, and with the development of future transport and energy systems.

Systems
