jobs.occupation: Senior Manager, Clinical Trial Disclosure & Transparency
jobs.description:
At Genmab, we are dedicated to building extra[not]ordinary® futures, together, by developing antibody products and groundbreaking, knock-your-socks-off KYSO antibody medicines® that change lives and the future of cancer treatment and serious diseases. We strive to create, champion and maintain a global workplace where individuals’ unique contributions are valued and drive innovative solutions to meet the needs of our patients, care partners, families and employees.

Our people are compassionate, candid, and purposeful, and our business is innovative and rooted in science. We believe that being proudly authentic and determined to be our best is essential to fulfilling our purpose. Yes, our work is incredibly serious and impactful, but we have big ambitions, bring a ton of care to pursuing them, and have a lot of fun while doing so.

Does this inspire you and feel like a fit? Then we would love to have you join us!

**Job Description

**Genmab is committed to transparency of clinical trial research. We recognize the scientific and ethical value of sharing clinical trial information in a non-biased and timely manner to benefit patients and other external stakeholders. The Clinical Trial Disclosure & Transparency (CTD&T) team resides within Clinical Trial Delivery, which hosts key functions for ensuring successful conduct and reporting of clinical trials.

We are now looking for a new Senior Manager to join our CTD&T team. The role offers a meaningful blend of operational and strategic tasks in a collaborative environment where quality, shared purpose, and cross-functional support are central to how we work.

In the role as Senior Manager of CTD&T, you will be executing against the global and national disclosure regulations and requirements across the entire Genmab portfolio. This role engages with internal and external stakeholders to ensure consistent and responsible disclosure and transparency practices. The position requires strong expertise in disclosure requirements and regulatory processes, coupled with strong organizational and communication skills, while maintaining a commitment to quality, integrity, and advancing Genmab’s mission.

**Responsibilities

**Your key responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

• Manage, track, and maintain overall responsibility for the disclosure of clinical trial protocols and results on ClinicalTrials.gov, EU CTIS, and other applicable registries/platforms.

• Support and provide guidance on redaction activities.

• Ensure development of plain language results summaries.

• Stay updated on industry guidelines to ensure compliance.

• Support in updating SOPs, contribute to process improvements, and maintain adherence to established standards.

• Oversee vendor performance related to transparency deliverables.

• Liaise with clinical CROs to ensure consistent messaging across study registries.

• Deliver training on Genmab’s disclosure processes to internal staff and provide guidance to CROs and vendors as needed.

• Ensure internal teams are informed of updated or new requirements and laws.

• Ensure management of unsolicited requests received via the clinicaltrials@genmab.com mailbox.

**Requirements

**

• 5+ years of clinical trial disclosure experience, including a Bachelor's or Master's degree with relevant specialization

• Strong knowledge of disclosure requirements, technology, and platforms.

• Proven ability to lead projects and facilitate cross-functional collaboration.

• Excellent written and verbal communication, that is effective, respectful, and concise.

• Previous experience as a Medical Writer is advantageous, given the close alignment between the CTD&T and Medical Writing teams.

For US based candidates, the proposed salary band for this position is as follows:

$132,800.00---$199,200.00

The actual salary offer will carefully consider a wide range of factors, including your skills, qualifications, experience, and location. Also, certain positions are eligible for additional forms of compensation, such as discretionary bonuses and long-term incentives.

When You Join Genmab, You’re Joining a Culture That Supports Your Physical, Financial, Social, And Emotional Wellness. Within The First Year, Regular Full-time U.S. Employees Are Eligible For

• 401(k) Plan: 100% match on the first 6% of contributions

• Health Benefits: Two medical plan options (including HDHP with HSA), dental, and vision insurance

• Voluntary Plans: Critical illness, accident, and hospital indemnity insurance

• Time Off: Paid vacation, sick leave, holidays, and 12 weeks of discretionary paid parental leave

• Support Resources: Access to child and adult backup care, family support programs, financial wellness tools, and emotional well-being support

• Additional Perks: Commuter benefits, tuition reimbursement, and a Lifestyle Spending Account for wellness and personal expenses

Further details on eligibility for compensation and benefits based on role will be provided during the recruitment process

**About Genmab

**Genmab is an international biotechnology company with a core purpose to improve the lives of patients through innovative and differentiated antibody therapeutics. For 25 years, its hard-working, innovative and collaborative team has invented next-generation antibody technology platforms and harnessed translational, quantitative and data sciences, resulting in a proprietary pipeline including bispecific T-cell engagers, antibody-drug conjugates, next-generation immune checkpoint modulators and effector function-enhanced antibodies. By 2030, Genmab’s vision is to transform the lives of people with cancer and other serious diseases with Knock-Your-Socks-Off (KYSO®) antibody medicines.

Established in 1999, Genmab is headquartered in Copenhagen, Denmark with international presence across North America, Europe and Asia Pacific. For more information, please visit Genmab.com and follow us on LinkedIn and X.

Genmab is committed to protecting your personal data and privacy. Please see our privacy policy for handling your data in connection with your application on our website Job Applicant Privacy Notice (genmab.com).

Please note that if you are applying for a position in the Netherlands, Genmab’s policy for all permanently budgeted hires in NL is initially to offer a fixed-term employment contract for a year, if the employee performs well and if the business conditions do not change, renewal for an indefinite term may be considered after the fixed-term employment contract.

Do you get excited by the shape of a whole world: the districts, the landmarks, the routes between them, and the little details that make a place feel lived in? Then you might be exactly who we're looking for.

Triband is the award-winning studio behind the WHAT THE? comedy game series, played by millions worldwide. From our home in central Copenhagen, more than 60 wonderful humans are united by a simple mission: to make everyone laugh.

We're growing! Triband is working on our most ambitious project to date: a new systemic open-world game built around a beloved IP, with our own spin on it. A bold new direction for us! And we're just getting started. Now we're looking for a Senior World Designer to plan, prototype, and build this world. You'll shape the big picture (the areas, how they connect, and how players find their way around) and work hands-on in the engine to bring it to life together with artists, designers, and the rest of your team. If maps and dots and their connections make you happy, you’ll probably like what comes next.

**Here's What You'll Do Day To Day

**

• Plan the world and lead its conceptualization, keeping a clear overview and vision for the whole map and for each new area before we start building it

• Create distinct spaces, biomes, and sections of the world (grounded in the real world), working closely with the art team to make each one feel unique

• Collaborate with artists and your team on environmental storytelling that gives each region its own identity

• Design how players navigate the world, using landmarks and the systems behind them

• Establish and maintain the world-creation pipeline, workflows, and hierarchy structures

• Work with developers on the tools that help build the world, such as traffic networks

• Gather needs from across the team and make sure they land in the right places in the world

• Build and implement hands-on in the engine like the rest of the team

**You're a great match if

**

• You have extensive in-engine experience. We use Unity, so that's preferred, but experience with other engines works too

• You've worked as a world or level designer on an open-world game as part of a team, and you know the common pitfalls of open-world design

• You have a strong macro-level design approach, balancing ideas and needs from different team members to create spaces that are believable, navigable, and fun

• You have experience establishing and maintaining detailed world and content documentation, and you like maps and spreadsheets

• A tidy hierarchy makes you happy, and you keep the small details and the big picture in view at the same time

• “Let’s try it out” is your favorite way to solve a problem

• You iterate on your work and stay open to changing it as the project evolves

• Balancing the needs of artists, designers, and programmers is a puzzle you enjoy rather than a chore

**Nice to have

**

• You enjoy building moment-to-moment, concrete level design too

• You can make people see a space before it exists, through a mood board, a rough walkthrough, or the story of a player’s first hour there

• You have an interest in urban planning and/or architecture

• You keep up with industry norms in open-world games

• You're drawn to casual, family-friendly, quirky universe building and storytelling

• You have experience prototyping mini games and activities

**What Always Matters To Us At Triband

**

• You thrive in taking ownership of your area: you spot problems, seek advice when needed, and implement creative solutions that push projects forward.

• You're motivated by collaboration, mutual respect, inclusiveness, and creativity, and you actively contribute to sustaining that culture.

• You believe games are made by teams, not solo rockstars, and that good ideas can come from anyone.

• You bring curiosity, generosity, and flexibility, along with strong opinions, especially when they come with reasoning, openness, and a willingness to actually test them.

• You're up for experimentation, and at the same time you don't get too precious when the experience tells you you're wrong.

• You value a positive work environment and contribute to keeping the studio a fun and supportive place.

**Practicalities

**

• We work on-site at our cozy office in central Copenhagen.

• This role is based in the Greater Copenhagen area, and we're not offering relocation for this one.

• We work a 37-hour work week, with core hours 10-15, and the freedom to start and finish anywhere between 7 and 18.

• Our working language is English.

• Most importantly: no crunch. People over deadlines.

**We offer

**

• A shot at shaping the world of a live game played by millions

• A tight, collaborative team where your ideas actually make it into the game

• A playful work environment where trying the silly idea is encouraged

• Friendly and kind colleagues who love making each other laugh as much as making games

• A professional development budget to invest in your growth

• Social activities like Friday bars, hobby nights, board game nights, and whatever else Tribanders turn into a tradition

• Daily lunch at a local restaurant, with plant-based options and soft ice on Thursdays

• Pension plan and private health insurance

• Child's first sick day on us, no questions asked

• Endless amounts of Cocio

**WHAT THE TRIBAND?**Triband is the award-winning studio behind the WHAT THE? comedy game series, played by millions worldwide.

From our home in central Copenhagen, more than 60 wonderful humans are united by our mission to make people laugh. We explore comedy through gameplay, which means we like to break player expectations, create surprising interactions, use great music and slick art, and build quirky worlds full of personality.

We put people first and strive to create a safe and creative working environment. We believe that teams, not individuals, make games. And we believe diversity makes teams better. For these reasons, we look for people who bring new perspectives and who are excited to challenge us and our way of doing things.

Factbird helps manufacturers turn real-time production data into decisions they can actually act on. Since 2016, we've helped manufacturers in 28 countries cut waste, boost uptime, and run smarter — from the shop floor to the boardroom. Over 300 companies trust us to make sense of their operations, and we're a team of 80+ people across Copenhagen and the US who care about making complex things simple.

We're creating a new role at the top of our Engineering career ladder: Lead Architect. It's the senior end of our Technical Track — the rung above Tech Lead — and today it's a role we've deliberately left lightly defined, because we want the first person in it to help define it. You'll set Factbird's technical direction: architecture, tooling, and the multi-year technology bets that shape where the product goes next.

This is our most senior technical role, with no direct reports — your authority comes from judgment and track record, not the org chart. You'll work alongside our Tech Leads in Factbird's technical leadership group, partner closely with our Director of Engineering, and be the person other senior engineers go to when a decision is genuinely hard to reverse.

About the Role

As Lead Architect, you own Factbird's company-wide technical vision: the architecture our services run on, the tooling and standards our engineers use every day, and the multi-year technology strategy that ties it all together. You make — or sign off on — the high-stakes, hard-to-reverse architecture calls, and you're accountable for getting them right with the full context of where the business is headed, not just where the code is today.

You'll work across a team built on Rust, React, Node.js, and AWS, with AI-assisted development already a core part of how we ship. Some of what this role owns is already well-defined — reviewing RFCs, stewarding language and platform standards, setting the team's AI-tooling strategy. Some of it isn't yet: Factbird is still a growing company, and part of the job is helping us figure out what technical leadership at this level should look like as we scale.

You'll thrive here if you'd rather be trusted with genuinely hard calls than manage a team, and if you can hold both the technical detail and the commercial context — cost, risk, market direction — well enough to make a technology bet you can still defend a year later.

What you'll do

Architecture & technical strategy

• Own Factbird's multi-year technology strategy, and make the high-stakes architecture calls that are hard to reverse — with cost, risk, and business context factored in, not just engineering elegance

• Author and drive major RFCs from proposal through to an actual decision, and review the highest-risk architecture changes across the team

• Act as steward for our core languages and frameworks — setting standards, library choices, and the platform's overall shape

• Make build-vs-buy calls for new technical capabilities, and bring a clear point of view on emerging technologies worth adopting

• Define the observability, reliability, and security posture the platform is held to

Tooling & standards

• Set the team's technical tooling and platform standards, and keep them evolving as the stack and the company grow

• Define Factbird's strategy for AI-assisted development — which tools we adopt, how we balance velocity against code quality, security, and IP risk, and where we draw the line

• Shape engineering-wide quality philosophy and help set the technical bar used in hiring interviews

• Help define shared components and reference architecture that other engineers build on, rather than reinvent

• Give input into technical org design and team topology as Engineering scales

Technical leadership & mentorship

• Act as the trusted technical advisor to our Director of Engineering and the technical leadership group, partnering with Tech Leads and Product Leads on cross-team alignment

• Mentor senior engineers and Tech Leads toward architect-level thinking, without formal ownership of their people management

• Communicate technical vision and trade-offs clearly to non-technical stakeholders, including leadership

• Identify technical risks to the business early, and say so before they become expensive

• Represent Factbird's technical thinking externally where it makes sense — a talk, a blog post, an open-source contribution — though this isn't a requirement on day one

What we’re looking for

We're looking for someone who's already earned this kind of trust somewhere else — someone whose technical opinions carry weight because they're right more often than not, and who'd rather solve the interesting, ambiguous problem than manage the team solving it.

The ideal background

• 8+ years of hands-on engineering experience, including real time spent as an architect or equivalent senior technical authority, not just a senior engineer with a bigger title

• A track record of owning multi-year technology strategy or platform architecture decisions that other teams had to live with — and that held up

• Has led major RFCs or architecture proposals cross-team, through genuine pushback, to an actual decision

• Comfortable making build-vs-buy and technology-adoption calls that account for cost, risk, and where the market is heading, not just what's technically interesting

• Experience mentoring senior engineers or Tech Leads toward architect-level thinking, without needing formal authority to do it

• Practical, current experience with AI-assisted development, and a clear point of view on where it genuinely helps versus where it creates risk

Why Factbird?

People are at the heart of everything we build. We believe great products come from empowered teams — and we work hard to create an environment where you can do your best work and have space for life beyond it.

Here's what you can look forward to:

• Flexible working hours: We trust you to manage your time. Life isn't one-size-fits-all, and neither is work.

• Competitive salary: We offer compensation that reflects your skills, experience, and impact.

• Internet reimbursement: Stay connected and productive, wherever you choose to work from.

• Thoughtful, human onboarding: We'll support you step by step, giving you the context, tools, and guidance you need to feel confident from day one.

• A career path that grows with you: Through bi-yearly Individual Development Plan conversations, we'll work together to shape a career journey that fits your ambitions.

• Company-wide gatherings & team days: We regularly come together across teams and regions to connect, celebrate, and align on what's next.

• A global, inclusive culture: We're proud of our diverse backgrounds and perspectives — and we actively celebrate them in how we work and collaborate.

We'd love to hear from you

If this role feels like a match, we'd be excited to hear from you and explore how you could help shape the future of data collection and production monitoring at Factbird.

jobs.occupation: Communications Student Assistant – Partnerships, Advocacy and Communications Team
jobs.description:
About ICARS    The International Centre for Antimicrobial Resistance Solutions (ICARS) is an independent international organisation established by the Danish Government to support low- and middle-income countries in developing evidence-based and context-appropriate solutions to antimicrobial resistance (AMR). Working across the One Health spectrum, ICARS collaborates with governments, research institutions and global organisations to bridge research, policy and implementation.    About the role   We are looking for a Student Assistant to join our Partnerships, Advocacy and Communications Team. This is a great opportunity for a student interested in digital communications, creative media, data management and global health and development. You’ll support our day-to-day activities and help communicate ICARS’ work on AMR in LMICs.   We’re looking for someone with strong technical skills who also takes initiative to bring fresh ideas to the team. Alongside delivering assigned tasks, you will be encouraged to suggest improvements and take ownership of agreed activities, with support and feedback from colleagues.      Key responsibilities    Website management:    	
•  	Maintain and update content on ICARS’ WordPress website, keeping it accurate, accessible and user-friendly.  	    	
•  	Track website performance using analytics tools and suggest improvements based on the findings.  	    	
•  	Proactively identify outdated content, gaps and opportunities to better showcase our work.  	   Graphic design & visual content:    	
•  	Create engaging infographics, social media graphics and report layouts that align with ICARS’ brand.  	    	
•  	Help develop templates and designs for reports and presentations, bringing fresh ideas for communicating complex information clearly.  	    	
•  	Video editing & multimedia:  	    	
•  	Edit videos for ICARS’ social media, presentations and events.  	    	
•  	Support video production and identify opportunities to turn existing footage into useful, engaging content.  	   Social media support :    	
•  	Support ICARS’ LinkedIn presence through content creation and community engagement.  	    	
•  	Keep an eye on relevant conversations, project updates and sector developments, suggesting timely stories and opportunities for ICARS to contribute.  	   Internal communications support:    	
•  	Maintain our internal SharePoint, including keeping our media library organised and up to date.  	    	
•  	Support colleagues with designing clear, engaging PowerPoint slides and formatting Word documents.  	   Press Office and external communications support:    	
•  	Assist with event promotion and Mailchimp newsletter creation.  	    	
•  	Monitor our communications mailbox, respond to routine enquiries and coordinate with colleagues on requests from stakeholders, including regional and national press.  	    	
•  	Flag relevant media and communications opportunities for the team to consider.  	   Data and stakeholder information management:    	
•  	Support the team in entering and maintaining accurate, up-to-date data and contact information in ATLAS, our CRM system.  	    	
•  	Other tasks related to deliverables of the Partnerships, Advocacy and Communications Team.   	      Desired profile    We are seeking an organised and curious student who enjoys both developing ideas and getting things done in a pro-active and structured manner. You take the initiative to find information, ask useful questions and suggest practical next steps. You can work independently, recognise when to seek guidance and lead tasks through to completion, while keeping colleagues informed. You are comfortable working in a fast-paced environment where priorities can change quickly, and you bring strong digital fluency, technical skills and the ability to pick up new tools with ease.   Required qualifications:    	
•  	Currently studying for a Master’s degree in IT, Media Studies, Marketing, Graphic Design or a related field.  	    	
•  	Proficiency in WordPress and basic website management.  	    	
•  	Experience using MS Office, particularly Excel, Word and PowerPoint.  	    	
•  	Experience with graphic design tools, such as Canva or Adobe Creative Suite.  	    	
•  	Basic video editing skills, using Premiere Pro, Final Cut or similar software.  	    	
•  	Strong organisational skills, working in a structured manner and with attention to detail.  	    	
•  	Ability to prioritise and manage multiple tasks.  	    	
•  	Ability to identify opportunities, propose ideas and take responsibility for delivering agreed tasks.  	    	
•  	Strong written and verbal communication skills in perfect and fluent English, including the ability to adapt content for different audiences.  	   Preferred qualifications:    	
•  	Knowledge of Google Analytics, or a willingness to learn.  	    	
•  	Experience using CRM platforms (Dynamics 365)  	    	
•  	Skills and interest in drafting technical and scientific communication material.  	      What we offer     	
•  	Hands-on experience: Contribute to drafting communications material, external stakeholder management and partnerships, developing your skills through practical work and feedback.  	    	
•  	Impact: Help communicate solutions to one of the world’s most critical global health and development challenges, with space to contribute your own ideas and see them put into practice.  	    	
•  	Flexible working hours: Our working hours between 8 am and 5 pm with accommodation of your academic schedule.  	    	
•  	International environment: Work alongside experts and colleagues from diverse backgrounds in a global organisation.  	   If you enjoy turning ideas into action and want to use your communications skills to support global health, we would love to hear from you!      Terms of employment   The position as student assistant will be covered by the terms of the collective agreement between The Danish Finance Ministry and the Organisation of Public Employees (OAO-S-Fællesoverenskomsten) and the organizational agreement between The Danish Finance Ministry and the Organisation for Salaried Employees HK/Stat (Organisationsaftale for kontorfunktionærer, laboranter og it-medarbejdere (HK)), according to chapter 6 in the agreement concerning hourly paid employees.   The successful candidate is enrolled at graduate level in a Danish University with at around two years of studies remaining. They will predominantly work from the ICARS HQ office, based at the Statens Serum Institut in Copenhagen, Denmark.      Application and recruitment process     Press “apply for the position” and submit your CV along with a cover letter outlining your suitability for the role and motivation for applying.     We would like to receive your application by 20 November 2026 and expect to conduct interviews 24-27 November 2026.   For questions about the role, please contact Communications Officer Chloe Modvig-Cole (checo@icars-global.org) and for other questions about the position you may contact Head of Partnerships and Global Relations Theresa Hogenhaug (tcah@icars-global.org). We are committed to cultivating a fair and healthy environment, where everyone can be themselves and thrive. We are happy to discuss flexible working options for all roles. We work to ensure that our recruitment processes are as inclusive as possible to everyone. This includes adjusting for people who have a disability or long-term condition.   We look forward to hearing from you!

jobs.occupation: Research Assistant in Artificial Intelligence for Power Electronics Design
jobs.description:
At AAU Energy, a fixed-term position as Research Assistant in Artificial Intelligence for Power Electronics Design, is open for appointment from January 1, 2027, or soon hereafter. The duration of the position is 2 years.

Your work tasksYour work will include developing, training and evaluating machine-learning models based on circuit data, board geometries, simulation results and design images. You will develop surrogate models that approximate thermal and electromagnetic solvers, enabling faster evaluation of design alternatives. The position may also involve computer vision for recognizing circuit structures, component placements and printed circuit board geometries from photographs or other images. In addition, you will investigate graph-based methods for representing circuit relationships, evaluating design rules and generating or testing hypotheses for circuit designs. You will contribute to the development and verification of agentic workflows, where artificial intelligence systems combine models, tools and design rules to reason through and support electronics design tasks. You will prepare datasets, document computational workflows, validate model performance and share results with colleagues working in artificial intelligence, power electronics, semiconductors and software development.

The position is offered within the research field of Artificial Intelligence for Power Electronics Design and contributes to AAU Energy’s focus areas of Digital Transformation and Artificial Intelligence, and Energy Efficiency in Components and Systems. The Research Assistant will be affiliated with the Section of Power Electronics System Integration and Materials.

Your competenciesYou have a relevant master’s degree in computer science, electrical engineering, electronics, artificial intelligence or a related field, and you are interested in working at the intersection of machine learning and power electronics design. You have a solid foundation in applied machine learning. Familiarity with electronic systems, including printed circuit boards, circuit topologies, components and the physical principles that influence electrical, thermal and electromagnetic performance, will help you engage with the engineering context of the role.

You have practical experience developing, training and evaluating machine-learning models, and you can translate complex engineering challenges into data-driven methods suited to a research environment. You are comfortable working with structured and unstructured engineering data, including circuit representations, board geometries, simulation data and images. Experience with computer vision, graph-based machine learning or graph neural networks will support your work with methods that interpret circuit layouts and geometries, reason about relationships between components, and generate or assess design hypotheses.

You are interested in developing surrogate models that approximate thermal and electromagnetic simulation tools while maintaining sufficient accuracy for use in electronics-design workflows. You work systematically with model validation, data quality and reproducible experiments, and you understand that artificial intelligence methods for engineering need to be technically robust as well as useful to domain specialists.

You communicate clearly in English, both in writing and dialogue, and you work well in a multidisciplinary environment where colleagues with expertise in artificial intelligence, power electronics and software development collaborate closely. You take responsibility for your tasks, ask constructive questions when assumptions need clarification, and contribute with curiosity and sound technical judgement to the development of new methods for intelligent electronic-system design.

Who we areAAU Energy is a research department at Aalborg University dedicated to the development of clean and sustainable energy systems. Our activities cover electrical, thermal and mechatronic energy technologies, and we work closely with industrial partners and other academic environments to address real-world energy challenges.

The department is located in both Aalborg and Esbjerg, and this position is based at the Aalborg campus. AAU Energy employs around 250 staff members at different career stages and from a broad range of national backgrounds. This creates an international and interdisciplinary research environment with many opportunities for collaboration and knowledge sharing. English is widely used as the working language in research and teaching, which makes it straightforward for international colleagues to integrate.

We offer access to advanced laboratory and workshop facilities and an environment where you can develop your academic profile through research, teaching and collaboration with both Danish and international external partners. As a workplace we value a collegial and inclusive culture with room for professional discussion, initiative and mutual support in everyday work.

New colleagues, whether they come from elsewhere in Denmark or from abroad, can draw on the university’s support services related to relocation, housing and practical matters. Aalborg University offers general onboarding support to all new employees, as well as dedicated support for international staff through its International Staff Unit (ISU). You can read more about relocation support and services here: https://www.en.hr.aau.dk/relocation-support

Aalborg University also offers Danish language courses to support international employees in settling into both the workplace and Danish society. International employees typically can attend Danish language courses during their first years in Denmark (depending on individual eligibility and national schemes).

You can read more about AAU Energy at www.energy.aau.dk

Qualification requirements Appointment as a research assistant requires academic qualifications at master's degree level.How to apply  Your application must include the following: 

• Application, stating reasons for applying, qualifications in relation to the position, and intentions and visions for the position. 
• Curriculum Vitae (CV). 
• Diplomas (master's degree diploma and potential PhD diploma). 
• Documentation of teaching qualifications (optional). 
• Additional qualifications in relation to the position. 
• References/recommendations. 
You can read more about the requirements for your application here.    

The application must be submitted via Aalborg University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aalborg University's website.  

Aalborg University wants to reflect the surrounding society and has diversity as a core value. Therefore, everyone, regardless of personal background and orientation, is encouraged to apply for the position. 

Aalborg University has a policy of parallel language use. International staff are encouraged, with support from the university, to learn Danish during their employment in order to support their integration into the workplace and Danish society. 

Danish language courses will be offered as part of the employment. 

Do you have any questions? If you have any questions about the position, you are more than welcome to contact us. You will find contact persons at the bottom of the jobpost.    

Selected candidates will be invited for an interview. Interviews are expected to be held during December 2026

Further information Read more about our recruitment process here   

The appointment process at Aalborg University involves a shortlisting process. You can read more about the shortlisting and appointment process here.  

The hiring process at Aalborg University may include a risk assessment as a tool to identify potential risks associated with new hires, ensuring the safety, compliance, and integrity of the workplace. 

Salary and terms of employment  The employment is in accordance with the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Universities and the Ministerial Order on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Universities. Furthermore, your terms of employment and salary are in accordance with the collective agreement between the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations and the state (AC collective agreement) and protocol on certain terms of employment of academic staff at universities.

You can find information about the salary and salary structure for the position in the Salary Overview for Recruitment - Scientific positions (VIP). Please refer to the introductory section of the page and the section entitled “Research assistant”.

There is a mutual probationary period of 3 months for the position.

Aalborg University - Knowledge for the worldAalborg University is an international workplace with more than 3,700 employees. We offer real-world-oriented education and create world-class research results through collaboration between researchers, students, and public and private companies. This is how we achieve insights, new solutions to societal problems, and knowledge that changes the world. Our main campus is in Aalborg, but we also have campuses in Esbjerg and Copenhagen.

About the job As HR Country Manager, you will be supporting Alfa Laval's Scaling for Future direction, with a focus on Denmark, with 2000 employees and five Danish legal entities. The role in this form is newly established, giving you a fantastic opportunity to influence the position and make it your own!  The position supports several types of organizations in Denmark and Scandinavia, such as sales companies, factories, shared services, business units, and product groups. The key priority will be to ensure HR alignment across the legal entities and compliance with Danish legislation and collective agreements. You will contribute to harmonizing people policies and practices and as a trusted partner, you will support and inspire management by proactively driving organizational, leadership, and competence development.  You will act as:     HR Country Manager for Denmark, ensuring alignment, compliance, and consistent HR practices across all five legal entities across four sites - Søborg, Kolding, Aalborg and Nakskov.     HR Representative in the Danish Country Council, coordinating national HR topics and providing a consolidated HR view to business leaders in the country council     HR Business Partner for Søborg Site Services and the HR Shared Services Scandinavia organization. Operational responsibilities:    Plan and drive national HR focus areas for the five Danish entities aligned with the business strategy and People Strategy.     Develop and implement people policies, processes, routines, guidelines, tools and analytics.     Ensure country-wide consistency for benefits frameworks, allowances, principles, policies.     Coordinate the salary budget and review process in Denmark together with the Employee Relations team in HR Shared Services     Drive, support and inspire management in organizational, leadership, and competence development.     Coordinate local HR activities at the Søborg site, including collaboration with employee representatives and relevant councils.  Travel is part of the job, mainly to our various sites in Denmark, but you will also have a few travel days a year within Europe. You will be part of the Danish Country Council management team as well as part of the Søborg Site Management team. You report to Per Lund Hansen, a manager who will give you freedom and mandate to perform at your best. jobs.description:
Do you have a passion for building strategic customer relationships and turning complex opportunities into long-term business success? Are you motivated by helping accelerate the energy transition through offshore wind solutions? If so, this could be your next career opportunity. At Semco Maritime, we are looking for an experienced Senior Sales Manager to strengthen our Renewables Service business. You will play a key role in developing strategic sales opportunities, supporting key customer relationships, and securing service contracts for offshore wind assets in selected international markets. Your position As our new Senior Sales Manager, you will have end-to-end commercial ownership of strategic sales opportunities within the Renewables Division. Working closely with customers, partners, and internal stakeholders, you will lead the external commercial journey from early opportunity identification and qualification through tender management, contract negotiation, award, and handover to project execution. At Semco Maritime safety is a core value, and in this role, you will contribute to maintaining and promoting a strong safety culture while delivering innovative solutions. Above all, your work will make a real change for the global energy sector. You will be accountable for building and converting a strong pipeline of strategic opportunities into profitable contracts while developing long-term relationships with selected key customers. You will shape winning commercial strategies based on customer needs, market dynamics, and Semco’s capabilities, and ensure that commercial priorities are aligned across relevant functions.You will contribute to defining our commercial focus for selected customers and market segments, helping ensure that we invest our efforts where Semco Maritime has the strongest position to win. Your success will be measured by your ability to build strategic customer relationships, develop high-quality pipeline and convert complex opportunities into sustainable and profitable business.Your place of work will be at our Global HQ located in Esbjerg, our office located in Copenhagen or our future office in Aarhus. The position is full-time, and you can expect to up to 30 travel days per year. Your tasks & responsibilities As our new Senior Sales Manager, you will take ownership of strategic sales opportunities throughout the entire commercial lifecycle.Working closely with customers, partners, and internal stakeholders, you will develop winning strategies, build strong commercial relationships, and identify growth opportunities across existing and new accounts. You will play a central role in shaping account strategies, developing customer-focused value propositions, and ensuring that commercial solutions are aligned with both customer needs and operational capabilities.In addition, you will represent Semco Maritime in customer interactions and industry forums, contribute valuable market insights, and help strengthen our commercial processes and best practices across the organisation.Your tasks will include but are not limited to: 
• Driving strategic sales opportunities from qualification through contract award and handover.
• Developing and executing winning strategies for key tenders and commercial opportunities.
• Building and maintaining strong relationships with strategic customers and supporting key account development.
• Leading customer negotiations in collaboration with technical, operational, legal, procurement, and finance stakeholders.
• Identifying and pursuing business growth opportunities, including cross-selling, upselling, and framework agreements.
• Ensuring high-quality commercial proposals, risk assessments, and governance approvals.
• Promoting a strong culture of safety, quality, compliance, and integrity in all commercial activities.Your profile & qualifications We are looking for a commercially driven professional who thrives in a customer-focused environment and has a proven track record of managing complex sales opportunities - preferably from the wind industry. To succeed in this role, we imagine that you: 
• Have significant experience with complex B2B sales, opportunity and tender management, contract negotiations, and the development of winning strategies for strategic sales opportunities.
• Bring experience from offshore wind, renewable energy, maritime, technical service, or related industries.
• Have a strong understanding of customer decision processes, competitive positioning, value creation, and commercial risk management.
• Have experience with key account management, account planning, and building long-term customer relationships.
• Are comfortable coordinating cross-functional sales and bid activities involving multiple stakeholders.
• Possess strong communication, presentation, and negotiation skills and work in a structured, proactive, and results-oriented manner.
• Communicate fluently in English, both verbally and in writing, and are willing to travel as part of the role. Welcome to Semco MaritimeAt Semco Maritime, we create change. For people. For projects. And for the global energy sector. With us, you will join a community of over 2,300 of the most dedicated thinkers and doers in the energy industry who are driving real change and making their own personal mark on the global energy landscape.While everyone knows why the energy transition is vital, we are concerned with the journey. How to get there. By providing the answers needed to make change real. Because we believe that global energy ambitions can only be realized through hard work and clever pragmatic solutions. This is what we do. This is what we invite you to participate in.Safety is at the core of everything we do, and we are committed to protecting our people, partners, and the planet as we work towards a sustainable energy future.So yes, working for us will change the energy sector – and may well change you too. We know that our people are our greatest strength. We strive to build an inclusive workplace where everyone can be themselves, contribute their perspectives, and feel part of the team. We welcome applicants from all backgrounds and believe that diverse teams help us find better solutions and move the energy transition forward.  Care to join the movement?Change. With us.Semco Maritime is an international engineering and contracting company with 2,300 employees and 40 years of dedication rooted in both the conventional energy sector and the offshore wind industry. This puts us in a unique position to bridge today's and tomorrow’s solutions, constantly seeking clever and pragmatic ways to realise global energy ambitions. We do this through comprehensive project management across all phases of energy projects together with world-leading partners across the globe.

Are you a night owl looking for a temporary warehouse job where you can earn money and gain valuable experience? Do you enjoy practical, hands-on work and prefer working at night? Then this could be the perfect opportunity for you!

We are looking for motivated and reliable warehouse employees to join the inbound department at Imerco, one of Scandinavia’s largest merchandise companies. As we head into the busy Black Friday and Christmas season, we need dedicated night shift workers to help ensure that incoming goods are received and handled efficiently.

The job

Your working hours will be from 23:00 to 07:00, Monday to Friday. The job starts in week 45 or 46 and includes training shifts. It is important that you are available to start during these weeks and can work through to the end of December.

It will be approximately full-time from November. This is a great opportunity to earn extra money while gaining valuable warehouse experience.

Your tasks in the inbound department include:

• 
Receiving incoming shipments

• 
Opening, lifting, and moving boxes

• 
Unloading pallets

• 
Working with the Autostore

We are looking for candidates who enjoy working at night and can stay focused and productive throughout their shifts. You should be comfortable with physical work, routine tasks, and a busy warehouse environment.

Additionally, we expect you to:

• 
Have experience working in a warehouse – experience with an Autostore is an advantage

• 
Be comfortable working night shifts from 23:00 to 07:00

• 
Prefer practical, hands-on, and structured work

• 
Be physically fit and able to stay active throughout the shift

• 
Be reliable, punctual, and able to work independently

• 
Communicate well in either English or Danish

We offer valuable warehouse experience during the busy Black Friday and Christmas season, along with the opportunity to earn money during the winter period. You will become part of a friendly and supportive team, where tasks are clearly defined and workflows are well structured.

Working hours, salary and location

• 
Working hours: Monday to Friday, 23:00–07:00

• 
Start: Week 41, including two consecutive training shifts

• 
Employment period: Through the end of December

• 
Salary: DKK 156.34 per hour, including Fritvalgskonto

• 
An ekstra 35 kr/hour when working the night shift

The warehouse is located in Vallensbæk, with good bus connections, nearby train stations, and free parking available.

Ready to join the night shift team?Apply today! We conduct recruitment on an ongoing basis and look forward to hearing from you.

Do you enjoy turning campaign concepts into sharp, engaging content for everything from CRM to Paid Media? And would you like to join a creative fashion environment where pace, quality and collaboration go hand in hand?

At SELECTED, we are looking for a Digital Graphic Designer to join our Brand Identity team while one of our colleagues is on maternity leave. 

YOUR TEAMYou will join our Brand Identity team and work alongside creative colleagues across graphic design, art direction, photography and other areas of brand communication.Together, we bring SELECTED's visual identity to life across channels and markets. Campaigns move quickly from idea to execution, so close collaboration, good creative sparring and the ability to keep several deliveries moving at once are part of everyday life.

YOUR ROLEYour main focus will be creating and adapting visual content for our digital channels, particularly CRM and Paid Media. You will take established concepts and translate them into strong executions across formats, platforms and markets, while keeping SELECTED's visual expression consistent.

More specifically, you will:

• 
Design layouts and visual assets for newsletters and CRM campaigns.

• 
Create and adapt artwork for Paid Media across platforms and formats.

• 
Resize and adjust creative assets for different channels and markets.

• 
Create moving content such as animations and short-form video.

• 
Support the wider creative team with ad hoc graphic design tasks.

• 
Help ensure a high and consistent visual standard across digital touchpoints.

YOUR BENEFITS

• 
See your work go live across channels and markets, from weekly CRM campaigns to Paid Media and moving content.

• 
Build breadth in your digital design experience, working across formats, platforms and different types of creative execution.

• 
Join a strong creative environment, where you work closely with colleagues across design, creative and marketing and have room to contribute with your creative perspectives within SELECTED’s established visual identity and creative direction.

• 
Enjoy flexible working hours and the opportunity to work from home as part of our way of working.

YOUR PROFILEYou are a skilled Graphic Designer with a strong visual eye and a feel for what makes digital content engaging and on-brand. You enjoy turning creative direction into strong executions and take pride in the details that make the final result come together.

We imagine that you:

• 
Have at least 2 years of experience in graphic design, preferably working with digital content.

• 
Are highly skilled in Adobe Creative Cloud, particularly Photoshop, After Effects, InDesign and Illustrator.

• 
Have a strong understanding of layout, typography and visual hierarchy, and experience creating content for digital channels.

• 
Work in a structured and detail-oriented way, comfortably managing several tasks and deadlines in a fast-paced environment.

• 
Experience with Figma, animation, motion graphics or short-form video is a plus. And if you have worked within fashion, lifestyle or another creative industry, that is an advantage too.

• 
Are comfortable communicating and collaborating in English in an international working environment.

WE LOOK FORWARD TO HEARING FROM YOUIf you have questions, you are welcome to contact Stephanie Widman on +45 30 85 36 42. Otherwise, send us your application, CV and portfolio as soon as possible and no later than 16 November 2026. We review applications on an ongoing basis and reserve the right to take the ad down, when we find the right candidate.

TERMS: The position is a one-year maternity cover with expected starting date on 1 December 2026.LOCATION: Brande, Denmark.
